clue.text: Strip of photomontage is transfixing discriminating type

indicators.note: a strip is a narrow piece cut from something longer, so the answer is a run of letters taken from the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of photomontage, through is and into transfixing

explanation.surface: A picture editor cutting a strip from a striking photomontage, admiring it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ageist is a person who treats people unfairly because of how old they are, a prejudiced type.

clue.text: Copy clothing little Parisian is liking

indicators.note: clothing means dressing or covering, so the copy word wraps around the French word

parts.note: to ape is to copy or mimic
petit is French for little, as a Parisian would say

explanation.surface: A copycat outfit for a small Parisian child is much admired.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite is a desire or taste for something, as in an appetite for adventure.

clue.text: In hearing, yours truly getting angry? I won't appeal

indicators.note: in hearing means as heard aloud, so the word for the setter is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: yours truly is the setter, who refers to themselves as I
sore is informal for angry or annoyed

explanation.surface: A defendant, angry at the hearing, declares that they won't take the case to appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom words hearing and appeal are a red herring; the definition is the eyesore speaking: I won't be attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, so it might say of itself that it has no visual charm.

clue.text: Maybe right song is to have a diverting effect?

parts.note: right is one example of a side, the other being left
a track is a song on an album

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the right song could take people's minds off things.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack is to distract someone from the main subject, steering their attention elsewhere.

clue.text: Scrambled eggs ultimately seasoned with Asian spices

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of eggs is used

parts.note: food cooked with Indian-style spice mixes is curried

explanation.surface: A breakfast of scrambled eggs finished off with a sprinkling of curry spices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled' looks like it describes the eggs, but it is the definition, in its sense of hurried.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble is to move hastily and awkwardly, just as one who scurried rushed along.

clue.text: The Reds storm up — Man City in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests things gone wrong, a sign the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A football report: Liverpool, the Reds, surge forward and Manchester City are struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reds sounds like a football team (Liverpool or Manchester United), but here it means communists. Man City is Manchester City football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Communists are commonly called Reds after their red flag, so the Reds can mean their political organisation.

clue.text: Follower of Liz Taylor is hiring houses

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tale of film star Liz Taylor taking on staff for her houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz Taylor the actress is a decoy: Liz is Liz Truss, UK Prime Minister in 2022, succeeded by Rishi Sunak.
explanation.definitionFit: Rishi Sunak took over as UK Prime Minister directly after Liz Truss resigned in 2022.

clue.text: Isaac's half-brother cooked his meal

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or, informally, falsified, a sign the letters are to be reworked

explanation.surface: A biblical domestic scene: Isaac's brother preparing his own dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Ishmael was Abraham's son by Hagar, so he shared a father with Isaac.

clue.text: Corrupt society girls swallowing a stimulant

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the society girls enclose the a

parts.note: debs are debutantes, young women entering high society
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Debutantes downing a drug, a corrupt high-society scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' reads as an adjective for the girls but is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase something is to lower its quality or morals, degrading it.

clue.text: Play a perfect match?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the title of a stage comedy by Oscar Wilde
second meaning: a flawless partner in marriage, the question mark flagging the playful literal reading

explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde's 1895 comedy has a title that, read literally, describes the perfect spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the title of a Wilde drama and literally describes a model married partner.

clue.text: Maybe George Eliot in rubbish dump? Yes and no

indicators.note: rubbish means worthless or poor, a sign the letters that follow are to be messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the novelist George Eliot to be found on a rubbish dump? A teasing yes and no.
explanation.walkthrough: George Eliot was the pen name of the novelist Mary Ann Evans. The fodder is DUMP, YES and NO; 'rubbish' is the anagram signal, not part of the dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen name is an assumed name an author writes under; George Eliot is a famous example, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Brother or sister keeping a hotel's address in India

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the sibling word encloses the other letters

parts.note: a sib is a sibling, a brother or sister
H is the abbreviation for hotel, as on maps and in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A sibling holding on to the address of a hotel for a family trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' is not a street address but a form of address, a title used when speaking to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: In colonial India, sahib was the polite title used when speaking to a man of rank, like sir.

clue.text: Frontrunner in triathlon went off and ran quite fast

indicators.note: the front runner of a word is its first letter, here of triathlon

parts.note: food that has gone off has rotted

explanation.surface: A triathlon leader who flagged and could only manage a moderate jog.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot is to run at a moderate pace, quicker than walking but short of a sprint.

clue.text: Where men go home amid Russian mountains

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the home word sits inside the mountains

parts.note: the Urals are the mountain range in Russia dividing Europe from Asia
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A description of where Russian men head for, at home among their mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Men's toilets have fixtures for men to relieve themselves, and 'go' is a euphemism for that.

clue.text: 50 per cent of this letter from Athens, or the next one

indicators.note: fifty per cent is a half, so the first half of the word this is taken

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, used in Athens

explanation.surface: A puzzle about Greek letters: half of one, or whichever follows it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by position: the answer is the Greek letter that comes straight after the one named in the wordplay, hence 'or the next one'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Greek alphabet theta is the eighth letter, directly following eta in sequence.

clue.text: Is the crossword setter with the Telegraph friendly?

parts.note: a setter calls themselves I or me; asked as a question, 'is the setter' becomes 'am I'
a cable is a telegram, sent by telegraph

explanation.surface: A question about whether the newspaper's own setter gets on well with the Telegraph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Telegraph' looks like the newspaper but means a telegraph message.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable describes relations that are good-natured and peaceable, as between friends.

clue.text: Maybe handbag thief's helper?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a handbag is an example of a fashion item worn with an outfit
second meaning: in law, someone who assists in a crime

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bag snatcher's helper; the two readings are a fashion item and an accomplice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an item that complements clothing and a person who aids a criminal.

clue.text: Road-user's problem in dull Phoenician city

parts.note: flat means dull or lifeless
Tyre was a major city of ancient Phoenicia, now in Lebanon

explanation.surface: A traveller's complaint about a boring ancient city on the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: The British spelling of tire makes the second word a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A deflated wheel from a puncture is a common breakdown for a motorist or cyclist.

clue.text: American's money stolen — this is taken by a gunman

definitions.text: this is taken by a gunman

parts.note: bucks is American slang for dollars
stolen goods are informally called hot

explanation.surface: A robbery: an American's cash is taken by an armed man.
explanation.walkthrough: The gunman seems to be the thief, but 'taken' means loaded into his gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshot is the coarse lead shot loaded into a shotgun cartridge, ammunition for a shooter.

clue.text: Confusing relation by author losing heart

parts.note: an uncle is a family relation

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so losing it leaves only the first and last letters of author

explanation.surface: A relative who writes books, but whose prose has lost its spark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear is hard to understand, muddled or ambiguous, so it confuses.

clue.text: Awful lice around head of Colossus in Rhodes, say

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the jumbled lice go on both sides of the single letter
awful means dreadful, a sign the letters of lice are to be put in a different order
the head of a word is its first letter, here of Colossus

explanation.surface: Dreadful lice crawling round the head of the Colossus of Rhodes, the ancient statue.
explanation.walkthrough: The Colossus of Rhodes leads to the island, but Rhodes here is Cecil Rhodes, the British colonial businessman; 'say' marks him as an example of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil was the first name of Cecil Rhodes, the imperialist after whom Rhodesia was named.

clue.text: Student follows half of course by old doctor, a French physicist

indicators.note: follows places the student letter after the half word
half of means the first three of the six letters of course

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A student taking half a course with an elderly doctor, studying a French scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb was an 18th-century French physicist who gave his name to the unit of electric charge.

clue.text: Tom's baby clothing put on figure

indicators.note: in a down answer, put on means placed above, so the clothing word sits on top of the number

parts.note: kit is a set of clothing, as in football kit
ten is a number or figure

explanation.surface: Someone named Tom dressing their baby and putting a number on its outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a male cat, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomcat is a male cat, and a young cat is called a kitten.

clue.text: Popular business with periodically immense earnings

parts.note: something popular is in
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter of immense is taken

explanation.surface: A trendy company boasting of its occasionally huge profits.
explanation.definitionFit: Incomes are the money people or firms receive, from wages or profits.

clue.text: E.g. radio and TV journo cutting plan up

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the journalist goes into the middle of the other word
in a down answer, up means read from bottom to top, so the word for plan is turned round

parts.note: to aim is to intend or plan
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A broadcast journalist scrapping a plan for coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio and television are examples of the mass communication channels collectively called the media.

clue.text: A sailor reported for military operation

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a salt is an experienced sailor, so 'a sailor' is 'a salt'

explanation.surface: A sailor has been put on report after taking part in a military action.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is an attack by armed forces on an enemy position.

clue.text: Maybe thistle, after time, becomes flower of Scotland

indicators.note: after places the weed word following the abbreviation for time

parts.note: a thistle is an example of a weed

explanation.surface: The thistle, given time, turns into Scotland's national flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower of Scotland' is the unofficial Scottish anthem, but here a flower is something that flows: a river. The Tweed forms part of the Scotland-England border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a major river running through the Scottish Borders, and crosswords use flower for river.

clue.text: No grand chef's art or science

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for grand is taken away

parts.note: gastronomy is the art of good cooking and eating
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An upmarket chef's cooking: is it an art or a science?
explanation.walkthrough: 'No grand chef' suggests a humble cook, but No is a removal signal acting on grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy is the scientific study of stars, planets and other bodies in space.

clue.text: Where William came from, and not Amanda

parts.note: nor means and not
Mandy is the short form of the girl's name Amanda

explanation.surface: A family story: William's birthplace, but not where Amanda came from.
explanation.walkthrough: William is William the Conqueror, the Norman duke who invaded England in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: William the Conqueror was Duke of the region in northern France from which he launched his invasion of England.

clue.text: I'm leaving a couple of runs for a cricketer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a farewell said on departure

definitions.text: a couple of runs for a cricketer
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batter untouched, so two are ...

explanation.walkthrough: A bye in cricket is a run added to the score when the ball beats both batter and wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled word is a casual goodbye, and also literally two of cricket's extra runs.
